_meta.note: Re-audit of the 22 S282 sources: caption-by-caption coverage check of the three PDFs and a page-by-page check of the web sources. Opus 5.5 card sections §3.4-3.5, §6.2, §6.5, §6.6.2, §6.6.4, §8.12.3 and §4 comparison cells; Table 8.1.A Fable 5.1 fills; AA v4.3 capability indices for GPT-6 tiers; AA Coding Agent Index components (Codex harness) from the AA launch post; MiMo report Table 7 (Distill-Qwen-9B per harness); Grok 4.7 AA fields, Grok 4.6 xAI column and CursorBench 4.0 chart points. Every value was checked against its cited line, RSC field or the rendered chart image.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic cyber classifiers — violative vulnerability-discovery flag rate
benchmarks.description: Share of sampled violative (binary-based, offensive-skewed) vulnerability-discovery traffic flagged by the model's own deployed safeguards (LLM-graded, privacy-preserving aggregation). Higher is better. System-level metric: model + its classifiers.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic cyber classifiers — defensive vulnerability-discovery flag rate (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Share of sampled defensive (source-code-based) vulnerability-discovery traffic flagged (blocked) by the model's deployed safeguards — a false-positive rate. Lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic rewind-attacker cyber adversarial robustness — attack success rate (lower better)
benchmarks.description: 133-task cyber-harmful suite (ransomware, exfiltration, real-CVE exploitation, C2, self-replication); a helpful-only attacker drives a Claude Code agent running the model with production safeguards, 400-call limit with rewind. Mean attack success rate over runs. Lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic RL training — successful reward-hack episode rate (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Training-time metric: share of RL training episodes (aggregated over the whole run) flagged by a general reward-hack classifier (Claude Opus 5 judge) on environments all three models share — not a post-release evaluation.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic RL training — successful "guessed the answer key" hacks (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Training-time metric: share of RL training episodes (aggregated over the whole run) flagged by a general reward-hack classifier (Claude Opus 5 judge) on environments all three models share — not a post-release evaluation. Subtype: final answer chosen by predicting the answer key.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic RL training — successful "copied a finished solution" hacks (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Training-time metric: share of RL training episodes (aggregated over the whole run) flagged by a general reward-hack classifier (Claude Opus 5 judge) on environments all three models share — not a post-release evaluation. Subtype: handed in existing work instead of producing it.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic RL training — successful "prohibited method or access" hacks (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Training-time metric: share of RL training episodes (aggregated over the whole run) flagged by a general reward-hack classifier (Claude Opus 5 judge) on environments all three models share — not a post-release evaluation. Subtype: used a ruled-out method or got past an environment restriction.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic RL training — successful reward-hack rate excluding the skipped-required-tool subclass (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Training-time metric: share of RL training episodes (aggregated over the whole run) flagged by a general reward-hack classifier (Claude Opus 5 judge) on environments all three models share — not a post-release evaluation. Excludes episodes where the model answered without a tool/code use the task required.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic RL training — reward-hack attempt rate on impossible (missing-file) tasks (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Training-time: share of RL episodes with at least one attempted reward hack on tasks whose environment was missing a needed file (two affected environments). Knowingly incomplete work counts as an attempt.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic RL training — successful reward-hack rate on impossible (missing-file) tasks (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Training-time: share of RL episodes with a successful reward hack on missing-file tasks.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic RL training — reward-hack attempt rate on intact tasks from the same environments (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Control condition for the missing-file tasks.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic RL training — successful reward-hack rate on intact tasks from the same environments (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Control condition for the missing-file tasks.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic — compliance with instructions planted in user-pasted text, Claude Code (max effort, lower better)
benchmarks.description: Coding evaluation: share of attempts in which the model executed, planned or passed on an attacker instruction planted in text the user pasted into their own message (all tool calls simulated). Max reasoning effort, no product mitigations.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic — compliance with instructions planted in user-pasted text, Claude Code (default effort, lower better)
benchmarks.description: Same evaluation at the model's default reasoning effort, no product mitigations.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic — destructive action rate in resampled Claude Code transcripts (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Internal employee Claude Code transcripts where a Claude model acted destructively (killing jobs, force-pushing, deleting sole copies) are truncated before the action and continued by each model (up to 8 actions, Opus 5 simulates tools and judges). Lower is better.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic — asks permission instead of acting destructively, Claude Code
benchmarks.description: Same resampling setup: share of continuations where the model asked the user (closing question or question tool) instead of taking the destructive action. Higher is better.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic self-preference (self-recognition) grading bias — no system prompt
benchmarks.description: Mean difference in 0–10 unacceptable-behaviour grades when the grader is told the transcript author is Claude vs another frontier model (positive = more lenient toward Claude). No system prompt. Closer to 0 is better.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic self-preference (self-recognition) grading bias — Claude-identity system prompt
benchmarks.description: As above, with a system prompt reminding the grader it is Claude. Closer to 0 is better.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic verbalized grader awareness — input clearly disclosed (autorater 8–10/10)
benchmarks.description: Share of sampled internal coding-evaluation transcripts where the model verbalizes awareness of a grader, restricted to inputs whose grading is clearly disclosed (autorater 8–10/10) per the autorater. Revised autorater (Sep 2026).

benchmarks.name: Anthropic verbalized grader awareness — input ambiguously disclosed (4–7/10)
benchmarks.description: Share of sampled internal coding-evaluation transcripts where the model verbalizes awareness of a grader, restricted to inputs whose grading is ambiguously disclosed (4–7/10) per the autorater. Revised autorater (Sep 2026).

benchmarks.name: Anthropic verbalized grader awareness — input barely or not disclosed (≤3/10)
benchmarks.description: Share of sampled internal coding-evaluation transcripts where the model verbalizes awareness of a grader, restricted to inputs whose grading is barely or not disclosed (≤3/10) per the autorater. Revised autorater (Sep 2026).

benchmarks.name: Anthropic — acts on a presumed grader in coding evaluations (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Share of scored transcripts (seven coding-evaluation configurations pooled) where the model changes its solution because of what it assumes about the grader. Derived from printed counts.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic — digs for evaluation/grader clues in coding evaluations (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Share of scored transcripts (seven configurations pooled) where the model searches the task for clues about graders. Derived from printed counts.

benchmarks.name: Rare-action calibration — strategy hint only (target 1%)
benchmarks.description: Serrano et al. 2026 replication: observed rate of a rare action the model is told to take 1% of the time, with a less leading strategy hint and no randomness source. 4,000 samples.

benchmarks.name: Rare-action calibration — no hint, no randomness source (target 1%)
benchmarks.description: Same evaluation with no hints or randomness sources. 4,000 samples.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic large-team eval — knowledge-base construction, single agent (0–1)
benchmarks.description: Agents read a company's documents and write an indexed knowledge base; score = share of held-out questions a reader answers correctly from the notes alone. Team size 1. 24-hour window, averaged over three attempts; quantitative results from a slightly different model version than the released one ("performance is comparable"). Fixed-team harness, one shared Linux machine, no network.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic large-team eval — knowledge-base construction, 100-agent team (0–1)
benchmarks.description: As above, team of 100 agents.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic large-team eval — Lean formalization, single agent (0–1)
benchmarks.description: Prove a challenging theorem in Lean from fixed statements; score = weighted share of 49 formal theorem proofs verified. Team size 1. 24-hour window, averaged over three attempts; quantitative results from a slightly different model version than the released one ("performance is comparable"). Fixed-team harness, one shared Linux machine, no network.

benchmarks.description: As above, team of 100 agents.
